subject: Emergency hold / backup purge schedule — exception request and evidence path
messages:
From: Carla Jennings <security@aurorahealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: ProcureOps <procure@procureops.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data retention & emergency purge window — follow-up

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for taking our call earlier. A couple of concrete asks from Aurora's compliance team: we need confirmation of the current backup purge cadence for customer snapshots and operational logs, and an option to place an emergency "do not delete" hold tied to our account for litigation/audit reasons. Specifically:

- Backups: what is the default snapshot retention window for production customer data (incremental snapshots and full exports)?
- Logs: retention for request/trace logs and system-level telemetry (including who can retrieve logs and the audit trail).
- Emergency hold mechanics: who is the approver, how quickly can we pause the purge, and what evidence will Redwood provide to show data preservation?
- Subprocessors: if you need to delay deletion, which subprocessors will touch the retained data (and are any cross-border transfers implicated)?

We'd like a short summary we can share with our legal ops. I'm attaching our list of secure questions (Aurora_DPA_SecureQuestions.pdf). Can you also confirm availability for a 30‑minute follow-up this week?

Thanks,

Carla Jennings
Security & Privacy Lead, Aurora Health
carla.jennings@aurorahealth.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Carla Jennings <security@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: ProcureOps <procure@procureops.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Data retention & emergency purge window — follow-up

Hi Carla — thanks for the doc. High level answers below; copying legal/procurement and infra for approvals/ops detail.

Summary (production defaults):
- Snapshots/backups: default retention = 30 days for customer snapshots stored in our hot S3-backed archive. Full export retention follows the same window unless an account-level exception is in place.
- Operational logs: request traces and service telemetry are retained 90 days by default; aggregated observability traces are 365 days for internal analytics (customer-identifying fields are redacted after 30 days by default).
- Emergency hold: we support an account-scoped temporary hold that pauses scheduled purge jobs and isolates the most recent set of snapshots. Activation requires an authorized request from the customer's legal or security lead + vendor approval from Redwood (infra ops + legal). Hold can be active within 4 business hours after approval; forensic snapshots are marked and immutable for the hold duration.
- Subprocessors & transfers: our standard subprocessors (cloud storage, logging provider, backup replication) are listed in the DPA appendix; any hold may require coordination with the storage subprocessor and could trigger cross-border replication checks depending on the region.

Evidence path: we will provide an immutable manifest and a signed timestamped attestation, and a direct drive folder with a snapshot manifest CSV listing snapshot IDs, commit times, and hash digests. For Aurora I'm provisioning the shared drive folder now: https://drive.redwood.company/shared/Aurora-legal-evidence

Immediate proposal:
1) Temporary extension: 60-day snapshot hold (instead of default 30) pending Aurora's formal request (legal ops).
2) DPA addendum: ProcureOps / Kimberly to coordinate a short addendum noting the hold duration and subprocessors impacted.
3) Cost & ops note: there is a marginal storage/replication cost for extending snapshot retention; infra will supply an estimate.

Attachments: redwood_snapshot_manifest_20270901.csv (placeholder manifest we will populate once hold is active).

Can Kimberly/Aditya/Connor confirm feasibility and any required approvals? Carla — if that sounds acceptable, I'll route the DocuSign addendum draft to ProcureOps and your legal contact. Happy to hop on a call today at 4pm PT if needed.

Best,

Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Security & Trust, Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0197

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 13:10:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Aurora ask — proposed 60-day hold and next steps

Team — looping you in to request approval for the customer exception. Key points below; please reply with explicit APPROVE / DENY and any conditions.

Context: Aurora (HS-87293) asked to extend the snapshot retention to 60 days and place an account-scoped "do-not-delete" hold while they complete an audit. They want a signed attestation and manifest.

Proposal:
- Grant a one-time 60-day snapshot hold starting when legal signs the addendum.
- Keep operational logs at 90 days (no change), but capture a forensic export of the most recent 90 days and store alongside the snapshot manifest in a legal evidence folder.
- Route a short DPA addendum (ProcureOps/Legal) that lists impacted subprocessors and the limited cross-border replication checks.
- Estimate incremental cost and bill to Aurora (one-time pass-through for additional storage + legal admin).

Operational asks:
- Connor: can infra mark the snapshots immutable and pause the purge jobs for this account? ETA to finish the work once approved?
- Aditya: estimate incremental storage/replication cost for 60-day vs 30-day retention (ballpark).
- Kimberly: is Legal/ProcureOps OK with the addendum text? Any redline blockers?

Quoting Carla's ask below for context:
> We need confirmation of the current backup purge cadence for customer snapshots and operational logs, and an option to place an emergency "do not delete" hold tied to our account for litigation/audit reasons.

Thanks — please reply by EOD so I can move forward with Aurora.

- Evelyn

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: ProcureOps <procure@procureops.com>, Legal Ops <legal-ops@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Internal: Aurora ask — proposed 60-day hold and next steps

APPROVE with conditions.

Conditions / clarifications:
1) DPA addendum: Legal will sign off on a 60-day hold limited to Aurora's account only. ProcureOps to prepare the DocuSign with clear scope and an expiry clause (60 days max unless a mutually agreed extension is executed).
2) Subprocessors: update the subprocessor appendix to flag the storage replication partner and the logging vendor. If any subprocessor will perform cross-border replication during the hold we must include an explicit transfer justification and a dataflow map.
3) Audit trail: Infra must produce the snapshot manifest CSV (IDs, timestamps, hashes), a signed attestation, and a tamper-evident log of the purge-job pause action.
4) Cost recovery: have Finance approve a one-time pass-through for incremental storage + legal admin; include a rough estimate before routing DocuSign.

Connor — please confirm ETA for marking snapshots immutable and pausing purge jobs (we need a clear ops playbook entry for HS-87293). Aditya — pls send a ballpark cost by EOD so we can include it in the addendum.

Once the two infra items and the cost estimate are in, ProcureOps will draft the addendum and route to Carla.

Kimberly Park
Director, Legal & Compliance, Redwood Inference
